reader.requirement: At --std 85 every CLOSE of a report file (plain, WITH LOCK, WITH NO REWIND, REEL/UNIT [FOR REMOVAL], several file-names, not open) updates that file's I-O status with the §1985:VII.1.3.5 value: 00 success, 07 for a phrase on a non-reel medium, 42 not open; a later OPEN of a file closed with lock gives 38.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector (2002+): at 85 the physical file is locked (any file-name's OPEN gives 38), from 2002 only the connector
DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility off at 85; SharedClose's lock release does not depend on it

reader.edition-search: grep IsActive/Edition in the FileRegistry Close paths and FileConnector.Close; no CLOSE arm in VersionConformancePass. The status assignment in CloseCell (Table 14 cell, the '42' guard, '07') is the same code at every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the CLOSE WITH LOCK lock scope (physical file at 85, connector from 2002) and WITH LOCK removed at 2023; the status update itself is the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover close forms and the 42 status on sequential files; not exercised: a report file (REPORT clause) through each format, several file-names in one CLOSE with one not open, CLOSE WITH LOCK then OPEN through another file-name

probes.printed: NOT-OPEN=42 OPEN=00 CLOSE=00 CLOSE-AGAIN=42 EXTEND=00 NO-REWIND=07 REEL=07 UNIT-REMOVAL=07 MULTI=00 00 MULTI-2=00 42 LOCK=00 REOPEN-LOCKED=38 OTHER-NAME-LOCKED=38 CLOSE-RP3=42; the USE procedure ran on each 42/38; report content DET1
probes.expected: §1985:XIII.4.2.4 GR4 with §1985:VII.1.3.5 values; GR7 each file-name updated; GR3 F (REEL on non-reel: file stays open); 38 for a physical file closed with lock

probes.printed: --std 2023: error COBOL0902: the CLOSE WITH LOCK phrase was removed in COBOL-2023
probes.expected: WITH LOCK is a phrase of 85 that 2023 dropped

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.4.2.4 GR4  (cite.py --check "causes the value of the I-O status associated with file-name-1 to be updated")
OK  §1985:XIII.4.2.4 GR1  (cite.py --check "A CLOSE statement may only be executed for a file in an open mode")
OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5  (cite.py --check "A CLOSE statement is attempted for a file not in the open mode")

reader.notes: Every CLOSE format goes through FileRegistry.CloseByFormat, which sets 42, 07 or the connector's close status from Table 14; report files take the same path. The 85 edition arm in this area, the physical-file lock, behaves as the 1985 text says.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-04/c6/r6.cob at --std 85 (a GLOBAL report file with a GLOBAL FILE STATUS item and a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR procedure), aimed at failed CLOSE forms and a contained program: CLOSE WITH LOCK of a file not open = 42 (USE ran) and the next OPEN OUTPUT = 00, so the failed CLOSE locked nothing; CLOSE WITH NO REWIND = 07 and the file is closed (the next OPEN OUTPUT = 00, not 41, GR6); CLOSE REEL, CLOSE WITH NO REWIND and CLOSE UNIT FOR REMOVAL of a file not open each give 42, not 07; a contained program INNER closing the GLOBAL report file updates the status item to 00 and a second CLOSE to 42, which the caller sees (AFTER-INNER=42); the outer program's non-GLOBAL USE procedure correctly does not run for INNER's CLOSE. cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.4.2.4 GR4 ('causes the value of the I-O status associated with file-name-1 to be updated'); OK §1985:XIII.4.2.4 GR6 ('the report file is removed from the open mode').
